Rental income prospects boost Grade A office market in Hong Kong's core districts
article:
The relatively swift recovery of Hong Kong’s Grade A office market has spurred some owners of properties in prime locations to accelerate the listing of their assets, analysts said.

Stanley Poon Chi-ming, managing director at Centaline Commercial, said the number of Grade A office properties for sale in core districts had increased, with the prospect of stable rental income from well-established finance, securities and banking players appealing to some buyers.

“Grade A offices have become the most sought-after asset class within the commercial and retail property sector, with a corresponding rise in the number of interested parties engaging in enquiries and negotiations,” he said. “Some owners say that it is better to sell now, even at a lower price, while there are buyers willing to step in. That’s why they have chosen this moment to offload their properties.”

An office with a gross area of about 2,449 sq ft on a high floor of the Far East Finance Centre in Admiralty was recently put up for sale with an asking price of HK$45 million ($7.36 million), or HK$18,375 psf, according to Midland Commercial.

Last week, the entire top floor of the 79-storey The Center in Central — owned by Shi Jinyu, the president of Giant Mind (China) — was listed for sale through an agency, market sources said.

They said the asking price for the property, which has a gross floor area of about 13,213 sq ft, was HK$400 million, or HK$30,273 psf, but they believed the final price would be much lower.

Shi bought the property for about HK$738 million in 2017, meaning the asking price is about 46% less than what he paid for it.

Poon said the prices of Grade A offices in Hong Kong had fallen by as much as 60% to 70% from their peak.

A study released by JLL on Oct 26 said overall vacancy rates in the Grade A office market had declined for a fifth consecutive month and stood at 12.4% at the end of September — the lowest level since May 2023.

Central recorded the most significant improvement among the major office submarkets, with its vacancy rate declining from 7.8% to 7.2%, mainly driven by leasing demand.

Sam Gourlay, the head of office leasing advisory at JLL in Hong Kong, said the city’s Grade A office market recorded a positive net absorption of 245,800 sq ft last month.

Vacancy rates for top-tier office buildings had continued to decline because leasing activity was focused on facilities in Central, Tsim Sha Tsui and West Kowloon, he added.

Data from Centaline Commercial indicates that the office property market recorded about 293 transactions in the third quarter of this year, up about 26% y-o-y, with total transaction value reaching about HK$6.127 billion, up about 12%.

Poon said that when attractive prices for high-quality properties offered desirable rental yields, some investors were keen to make purchases.

“This is because most Grade A office buildings are held by developers or major landlords as long-term rental assets,” he said. “It is quite rare for them to be subdivided or sold off in parts. Properties with high profiles that are also available for sale are even scarcer.”

Kelvin Li, director at Midland Commercial, said he expected more Grade A office properties would be put on the market.

“Owners may have different reasons for bringing assets to market, including recycling capital, managing financing needs or rebalancing their portfolios,” he said. “However, the recent availability of prime office properties in Central and Admiralty does not necessarily imply a continued flow of heavily discounted assets across the board.”

title: Behind the Sheraton sale: A window into Hong Kong’s new restructuring reality
article:
The HK$2.7 billion ($440 million) sale of two Shimao Group hotels in Hong Kong leaves an estimated HK$1.8 billion shortfall against their secured loans.

Still, receivers managed to squeeze out improved bids in the final stages, with all shortlisted parties improving their offers, says Una Ge, a managing director at AlixPartners who oversaw the sale as a joint receiver.

The deal offers a glimpse into how mainland China’s developer debt crisis is reshaping Hong Kong’s restructuring industry, bringing vastly larger debt burdens, cross-border contagion risks, and increasingly complex creditor syndicates.

Resolving distressed debt in today’s frozen market is no simple matter of selling real estate, Ge says in an interview with the South China Morning Post .

When AlixPartners took over the 1,219-room complex in Tung Chung in June, its mandate was to protect a live hospitality business from liabilities linked to distressed mainland Chinese developer Shimao, while managing a transaction involving more than 1,000 contracts, Ge notes.

Under agreements signed in late October, the Sheraton Hong Kong Tung Chung Hotel and Four Points by Sheraton will be acquired by Oceanfront Hong Kong, which is controlled by Malaysian property developer ParkCity Group.

Shimao initially sought between HK$6 billion and HK$6.5 billion for the assets in 2023, before lowering its expectations to HK$4.5 billion late last year.

The final HK$2.7 billion sale price represents a 40% haircut to the HK$4.5 billion syndicated loan facility — originally led by lenders including HSBC — illustrating the steep concessions banks are making to reduce balance-sheet pressure and limit provisioning.

Preserving operating cash flow was central to the transaction. AlixPartners worked with Marriott International to ensure operational continuity before court orders were formalised, reflecting the reality that hotels are operating businesses rather than passive real estate assets.

“A lot of communication took place before we were formally appointed, and we had the support of the Marriott team,” Ge says. Maintaining “business as usual” was “critical” for prospective buyers and for lenders deciding whether to support the sale.

That operational stability helped preserve buyer conviction, Ge says.

While borrowers in offshore receiverships often dig in their heels and resist creditor enforcement, Ge says Shimao was cooperative from the outset, providing information and agreeing to publicly confirm in its Hong Kong stock exchange disclosures that the hotels would continue operating normally.

The confirmation was important for reassuring customers that existing bookings, including wedding banquets, could proceed as planned, Ge says.

Shimao’s cooperation in the hotel receivership followed its earlier efforts to reduce liabilities through orderly disposals in Hong Kong, including the sale of mortgaged office floors in Central’s landmark skyscraper, The Center.

The legal mechanics were equally challenging and involved far more than transferring ownership of the buildings. “This is effectively an M&A (mergers and acquisitions) deal,” Ge says. “The hotel company has existing contracts and obligations that come with it.”

Working with A&O Shearman and Marriott’s regional M&A team, the receivers drafted two interconditional agreements separating the physical assets from the operating entities. The structure allowed the Malaysian buyer to assume control without inheriting Shimao’s broader corporate debt obligations.

The transaction required novating more than 1,000 commercial agreements and securing consents under Marriott’s long-term management contract.

Because day-to-day operations would remain with the hotel brand, whoever bought the asset “needed to have real confidence in Marriott’s ability to run the hotel”, Ge says.

The tender drew formal interest from buyers across nine markets, including mainland China, Singapore, Malaysia, Japan, Australia, Europe, the Middle East and the US. Following the initial tender, receivers asked shortlisted parties to revise their terms, and all submitted higher offers.

Ge notes that decisions in such processes were not based solely on price, with execution certainty, financing commitments and board approvals also carrying significant weight.

On the ground, the receivers took direct management of the adjoining T Bay shopping mall, renewing retail leases, upgrading signage and launching guest-discount programmes.

“Anything that adds value, we are willing to go the extra mile for,” Ge says, adding that monthly hotel revenue posted y-o-y gains throughout the sale process.

An 18-year restructuring veteran, Ge says that while the legal tools available to advisers remained broadly unchanged, the scale of Chinese developer defaults had expanded the network of offshore stakeholders beyond anything seen in previous cycles.

As for whether commercial property had reached a bottom, Ge observes that prime office leasing in Central had shown initial signs of stabilising, though it remained unclear how quickly improvement could spread to non-core districts.

Capital values, however, remained under pressure. For property owners and lenders weighing whether to hold or sell, Ge says historical acquisition costs should not drive decision-making.

“People tend to anchor on their sunk cost, which is the original investment. But that may not be so relevant when making forward-looking decisions,” she adds.

According to Centaline Property, lenders were increasingly turning to mortgagee sales to recover cash, while office buildings continued to trade at discounts, with some offered at 20% to 25% below original purchase prices.

With lenders increasingly turning to forced sales to recover their money from distressed properties, Ge says a borrower’s willingness to work towards a resolution could influence how lenders approached a distressed situation.

“If banks see that a borrower is genuinely working hard to improve the situation, in my experience, they are more willing to give their support,” she says.

title: UOB prices 38 Marina Collection units from $1,269 psf, below recent Sentosa Cove resales
article:
UOB is selling 38 apartments at Marina Collection in Sentosa Cove at prices starting from $1,269 psf, following a long-running legal dispute involving defaulted housing loans at the development.

The 124-unit Marina Collection is one of 10 luxury condos in the prime 99-year leasehold waterfront residential enclave of Sentosa Cove. Together, they comprise 1,766 units.

As at Oct 27, there had been 62 resale transactions across the 10 developments this year, based on caveats lodged.

Excluding three substantially larger and pricier transactions at Seven Palms Sentosa Cove , including one involving two combined units, the remaining 59 resales averaged $1,672 psf.

The 17 three-bedroom and 21 four-bedroom units now offered for sale at Marina Collection average about $1,340 psf, 20% below the average resale price across Sentosa Cove this year.

“The pricing has been strategically positioned to offer buyers an attractive entry point into Sentosa Cove’s exclusive waterfront residential market,” says Dominic Lee, head of the luxury team and investment sales at PropNex, the sole marketing agent.

“We believe this presents a compelling opportunity for discerning buyers seeking long-term value in one of Singapore’s most prestigious residential enclaves.”

Lee points out that the average price is even lower than the $1,537 psf per plot ratio (ppr) paid for a 99-year leasehold Government Land Sale site at New Upper Changi Road in September. “That’s just for land, and in the suburbs, in the Outside Central Region,” he says.

Marina Collection, by contrast, is located in Sentosa Cove, District 4, within the Core Central Region.

Below market prices

UOB’s starting price is also lower than previous developer promotions in the precinct. Ho Bee Land Limited offered the last 16 units at Turquoise from $1,290 psf in April 2021, while Cityview Place Holdings, an associate company of City Developments Ltd (CDL) , relaunched The Residences at W Singapore Sentosa Cove from $1,648 psf in April 2024.

As at Oct 27, 18 units had changed hands at The Residences at W Singapore Sentosa Cove this year, at prices ranging from $1,783 to $1,985 psf. Meanwhile, three units at Seascape were sold at prices ranging from $1,549 to $2,080 psf.

Two units at Cape Royale , Sentosa Cove’s largest condo with 302 units and its tallest, at 17 to 20 storeys, sold for $1,846 and $2,148 psf.

What’s on offer

Among the 38 Marina Collection units, the three-bedroom apartments range from 1,873 sq ft (without private enclosed space or PES) to 2,099 sq ft (with PES). Asking prices start from $2.588 million ($1,381 psf) to $2.786 million ($1,327 psf).

The four-bedroom condos range from 2,185 sq ft (without PES) to 2,390 sq ft (with PES). They are priced from $2.948 million ($1,349 psf) to $3.11 million ($1,301 psf).

Of the 38 units, 12 are vacant, while the remaining 26 are tenanted, with leases expiring between 4Q2026 and 4Q2028.

According to Lee, the three-bedroom units command monthly rents of $8,400 to $9,000, while the four-bedroom apartments are rented out from $10,500 a month. Based on the asking prices, estimated gross rental yields range from 3.7% to 4.3%. According to Lee, the yields are “extremely attractive”.

After factoring in monthly maintenance charges of $1,734 for three-bedroom units and $1,951 for four-bedroom units, indicative rental yields at Marina Collection would range from 2.9% to 3.5%, before property tax and other expenses.

The units are being sold on an “as is, where is” basis. The preview runs from Nov 6 to 13, with sales bookings scheduled for Nov 14.

Buyers pay a 1% option fee, followed by another 4% upon exercising the option within two weeks. The remaining 95% is payable upon completion within eight weeks. UOB will provide financing of up to 75% of the purchase price.

End of a long legal dispute

The sale follows the conclusion of UOB’s long-running lawsuit against Lippo Marina Collection, the developer of Marina Collection on Cove Drive.

In October 2022, the Appellate Division of the High Court found the developer liable for conspiring with purchasers to mislead UOB into disbursing inflated housing loans for 38 units sold between 2011 and 2013.

According to court documents, the developer offered buyers undisclosed “furniture rebates” of 22% to 34% after property cooling measures slowed sales, while purchase documents reflected higher prices. UOB disbursed about $182 million in housing loans, in some cases exceeding the amounts buyers actually paid for their properties. All 38 buyers subsequently defaulted on their loans.

In July 2025, the High Court awarded UOB $17.7 million in damages. On Aug 24, 2026, the Appellate Division increased the award to $76.1 million. The amount was subsequently corrected to approximately $82.4 million to account for interest that had been omitted.

Launch buyers sell at a loss

Marina Collection was launched by the developer in December 2007, when units sold for $2,636 to $2,881 psf. Prices peaked at $2,912 psf in January 2008, when a 2,185 sq ft, four-bedroom apartment fetched $6.36 million, according to caveats lodged.

Completed in 2011, the development has approximately 79 years remaining on its 99-year lease.

All four units that changed hands at Marina Collection this year were sold at losses of 32% to 46% from their original purchase prices.

The biggest loss involved a 4,725 sq ft penthouse purchased for $12.67 million ($2,681 psf) in January 2008 and sold for $6.8 million ($1,439 psf) in September. The seller incurred a loss of $5.87 million, or 46.3%, after holding the property for almost 19 years.

In early October, a four-bedroom apartment sold for $3.1 million ($1,419 psf), down 43.2% from its $5.46 million ($2,500 psf) purchase price in February 2010.

Two three-bedroom apartments, each measuring 1,873 sq ft, also changed hands this year. One went for $2.8 million ($1,495 psf) in April, while the other went for $2.78 million ($1,484 psf) in June. Their sellers incurred losses of 32% and 43.8%, respectively.

Meanwhile, the developer has continued selling its remaining units and now has just one apartment left: a 3,789 sq ft, four-bedroom duplex penthouse with a private pool, priced at $6.5 million ($1,715 psf). PropNex is also marketing this unit.

Singaporean buyers to dominate

Lee expects Singaporeans and permanent residents (PRs) to account for the majority of buyers, similar to the profile at the relaunch of The Residences at W Singapore Sentosa Cove in April 2024.

Cityview Place Holdings reported that Singaporeans and PRs accounted for 94% of buyers at the relaunch. The remaining 6% were foreigners from China, France and the US.

The buyer profile for The Residences at W Singapore Sentosa Cove reflects a shift in demand at Sentosa Cove towards local purchasers, particularly after the April 2023 cooling measures raised additional buyer’s stamp duty (ABSD) for foreigners to 60%.

For the 120 Sentosa Cove condo units PropNex has sold since 2016, Singapore citizens and PRs accounted for 75% of buyers, while non-PR buyers made up about 24%, according to the agency’s sales data.

Under Singapore’s free trade agreements, US nationals, as well as nationals and PRs of Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway and Switzerland, enjoy the same ABSD treatment as Singapore citizens. This means qualifying buyers pay no ABSD on their first residential property purchase. US citizens therefore accounted for the largest share of foreign buyers.

Buying to stay

Lee expects most buyers of the UOB units to be owner-occupiers, although some may purchase for investment or as a trophy asset.

Units at Marina Collection overlook the swimming pool, the neighbouring One°15 Marina and the sea beyond. The development is also within walking distance of the waterfront restaurants and lifestyle amenities at Quayside Isle.

“The appeal of Sentosa Cove is that you don’t feel like you’re in Singapore, but in another part of the world,” says Lee.

He adds that Marina Collection offers buyers an attractive entry point into that lifestyle.

title: From Tuas To NTU And Sydney, This Company's Latest Growth Plans Take Shape
article:
October 2026 has seen Wee Hur Holdings make three key operational announcements.
Two announcements give investors greater certainty over an established income source, and a sizeable new opportunity in student accommodation -- all in Singapore.
The third announcement is about a development project in Sydney to create student accommodation.

Its Tuas View Dormitory lease extension protects an operating asset, while the Nanyang Technological University (NTU) project offers new growth potential.
Together, these announcements strengthen Wee Hur’s strategy of building recurring income alongside its construction and property development activities.

Keeping a major earner going

On 27 October, Wee Hur
announced
that JTC had extended Tuas View’s land lease by
two years and eight months
, from 1 November 2026 to 30 June 2029.

The significance is its scale.
Tuas View’s
15,744 beds
represent about 60% of the group’s 26,244 worker accommodation beds. Losing the right to operate such a large asset would have threatened a substantial part of its accommodation business.
Tuas View averaged 92% occupancy in the first half of 2026, with stable rents.
Wee Hur says Tuas View already meets interim dormitory standards, allowing operations to continue without disruption to residents and their employers.

Tuas View averaged 92% occupancy in the first half of 2026, with stable rents.
Wee Hur says Tuas View already meets interim dormitory standards, allowing operations to continue without disruption to residents and their employers.

“The extension of Tuas View Dormitory reflects the trust built over more than a decade of operating one of Singapore’s largest workers’ dormitories. It gives us continued income visibility from an established asset and reinforces our workers’ dormitory business as a stable source of recurring income for the Group.”
–
Goh Chengyu, CEO, Wee Hur Property

Meanwhile, the new 10,500-bed Pioneer Lodge is filling up.
Wee Hur says occupancy is expected to reach 97% on 1 Nov, compared with an average of 66% in 1H2026. More occupied beds should support its rental income.

The workers’ dormitory division generated
S$63.3 million of revenue in 1H2026, up 50.7%
from a year earlier.

NTU opens another door

Announced on 16 October, the
NTU award
covers approximately
1,398 student beds
, mainly for postgraduates. It will be Wee Hur’s first Y Suites property in Singapore, extending its student housing business beyond Australia and Hong Kong.

For perspective, Wee Hur’s UniLodge Park Central development in Brisbane has 1,578 beds. NTU would therefore rank among its largest individual student accommodation projects.

Wee Hur will design, build, finance, operate and maintain the development. This gives it an opportunity to apply its experience across the property cycle and earn accommodation income over time.

To help finance the project, Wee Hur expects to lend S$60 million to the project company, in which it owns 80%. That commitment represents approximately 9.4% of its latest audited net tangible assets, as measured at 31 December 2025.

The S$60 million is capital Wee Hur plans to provide to the venture. Neither the construction contract value nor the total development cost has been disclosed.

Construction is targeted for 3Q2027, with operations expected by the
2029/30 academic year
. The definitive agreement is still being finalised, and the project is subject to approvals.

The proposed initial land lease is 20 years, with options for two further five-year terms.
At 1HFY26 results briefing (L-R): CIO Goh Wee Ping, Executive Chairman Goh Yeow Lian, CEO Wee Hur (Australia) Scott Peter William.
Photo: Company
The NTU news was followed by another one about Wee Hur
securing an unconditional option
for the proposed acquisition of a 2,744 sqm site at 35–51 Nicholson Street, Wollstonecraft, Sydney, with acqusition completion expected in 2H2027.
The site is earmarked for a 12-storey, 471-bed purpose-built student accommodation.

while NTU and Sydney projects create potential new sources of income.

The eventual contribution from the new student accommodation projects will depend on development costs, financing terms, rental rates and occupancy.

Wee Hur is positioning itself for a larger, more diversified recurring-income business, with multiple avenues for growth across Singapore, Australia and Hong Kong.

title: SGX Shares Have Been a Big Winner: Is It Still a Buy Today?
article:
Singapore Exchange
(SGX: S68) has been on a strong run in 2026, delivering solid capital appreciation alongside steady payouts.
Surging trading activity, a revived domestic stock market, and policy moves to boost liquidity have provided clear tailwinds.
As Singapore’s sole equity exchange with an expanding moat across FX and derivatives, SGX sits right at the heart of the country’s financial engine.
Yet after such a strong run, investors have to ask: is future growth already priced in, or is there still value left on the table?
What is Driving SGX’s Earnings Surge?
SGX’s stock rally was caused by a sharp rebound in local market activity.
Over the past year, total shareholder returns were propelled by a 34.9% jump in Securities Daily Average Traded Value (SDAV) to S$1.8 billion, driving cash equities revenue up 28.1% to S$502.9 million.
Beyond traditional stock trading, currency clearing reached record volumes, pushing FX net revenue up 12% to S$126.6 million as average daily volume hit US$190.2 billion.
This multi-asset diversification gives the exchange a recurring earnings cushion whenever equity turnover cools down.
Efforts by the Singapore government to deepen market liquidity and attract new growth listings have provided additional structural tailwinds.
If these capital market reforms permanently channel institutional capital into local shares, SGX stands to collect steady clearing and listing fees for years to come.

For FY2026, SGX raised its regular dividend to S$0.445 per share, an 18.7% increase over FY2025.
Management also declared a one-off capital return dividend of S$0.125 per share, bringing total FY2026 distributions to S$0.570 per share.
Furthermore, management has guided for planned quarterly dividend increases of S$0.0025 through FY2028.
At a recent share price of around S$20.73, the regular dividend of S$0.445 provides a baseline yield of approximately 2.15%, which increases to roughly 2.75% when factoring in the one-off distribution.
SGX’s dividend growth is backed by strong cash generation and a conservative balance sheet.
Regular dividend distributions are fully supported by FY2026 adjusted net profit of S$759.5 million, leaving a comfortable payout ratio below 63% on ordinary dividends.
SGX is best understood as a
defensive compounder
operating with high capital efficiency.
At a 2.15% regular yield, it’s lower than a 10-year Singapore Savings Bond.
Similarly, its targeted medium-term revenue growth of 6% to 8% positions it as a steady rather than high-beta growth stock.
Related articles:
3 Singapore Stocks That Have Raised Their Dividends Consistently Over the Past 5 Years
3 Singapore Blue Chips Raised Their Quarterly Dividends by Up to 25%
Is SGX Still Attractively Valued After Its Rally?
At around 29.2x adjusted trailing earnings, SGX trades well above its historical 5-year average P/E range of 21x to 23x.
The market pays this premium for SGX’s earnings stability, cash conversion, and wide regulatory moat.
However, trading near the top of its historical valuation band leaves little margin of safety.
While FY2026 adjusted EPS jumped 24.6% to S$0.71, the stock’s multi-month price advance outpaced underlying profit growth.
A significant portion of recent total returns came from valuation expansion, where investors paid progressively more per dollar of earnings rather than relying solely on profit growth.
What Could Go Wrong for SGX?
In the near term, SGX’s revenue remains tied to market sentiment and daily traded volumes.
Offering more asset classes can help soften the blow when things slow down, but when the market stays quiet for a while, the cash equities clearing fees always take a hit.
At the same time, SGX isn’t the only game in town.
Global and regional rivals are all fighting hard to attract international listings.
If trading volumes don’t bounce back quickly or if new market initiatives take longer than planned to attract fresh liquidity, the share price could take a real hit.
Conclusion – Get Smart: Is SGX Still Worth Buying?
SGX remains a strong business with a dominant market moat and expanding multi-asset momentum.
Yet after a sharp rally, its operational strength looks fully priced in.
Even an outstanding company makes a poor investment when bought at too high a valuation.

Looking past top-line numbers reveals the underlying cash and operational shifts that matter.
Micro-Mechanics posts a record quarter
Micro-Mechanics makes precision consumable tools and parts used in semiconductor manufacturing.
For 1QFY2027 ended 30 September 2026, revenue rose 45.0% year on year (YoY) to an all-time quarterly high of S$24.2 million, while net profit more than doubled, climbing 102.8% to S$6.4 million.
Build-to-Print sales nearly doubled – up 97.5% YoY – helped by higher bookings and a recovery from prior material shortages.
Consumable Tools grew 33.7%.
Profitability also strengthened as gross margin widened to a 20-quarter high of 55.0% from 51.5% a year ago.
Despite record earnings, free cash flow slipped 10.6% to S$3.7 million as trade receivables grew alongside sales, tax payments increased, and capital expenditure more than doubled to S$0.9 million.
The company maintained a
healthy balance sheet
with S$33.3 million in cash and zero bank borrowings.
No dividend was declared, in line with its usual practice of distributing dividends only in the second and fourth quarters.
Management is pressing forward with a five-year strategy to double revenue from FY2026 levels to at least S$150 million.

Info-Tech Systems delivers steady revenue growth
Info-Tech Systems is a software-as-a-service provider offering cloud-based human resource management, accounting, and CRM software to over 28,000 businesses across five countries.
For the first nine months of 2026 (9M2026), revenue rose 20% YoY to S$42.6 million, with third-quarter revenue climbing 18% to S$15.3 million.

Subscription revenue grew 11% to S$32.2 million, led by a 26% increase in Malaysia.
The Services unit surged 82% to S$8.6 million, propelled by strong demand for AI-related courses at its Academy.

Management expects stable full-year growth and plans to launch its Academy in Malaysia before the end of FY2026.

For 9M2026, revenue edged up 1.6% to US$134.5 million, but net property income (NPI) fell 4.3% to US$64.8 million, and distributable income slipped 1.1% to US$34.8 million.
This contraction stemmed mainly from the redevelopment of 8217 Linton Hall Road and softness in Los Angeles.
Portfolio occupancy dipped slightly to 97.0%.
Despite lower NPI, leasing momentum remained resilient, with new and renewal leases achieving a 23% positive cash rental reversion.
Management also bought back 27.4 million units, adding 1.0% to distribution per unit (DPU).
The REIT agreed to sell its entire 90% interest in its Toronto data centre to its sponsor,

title: Uniqlo scraps price rise on US$2 socks after Japan shopper outcry
article:
(Oct 29): Uniqlo ditched plans to raise the price of its popular ¥290 (US$1.84) socks, underscoring the challenge Japanese retailers face as persistent inflation squeezes household budgets.

Earlier this month, the apparel brand, owned and operated by Fast Retailing Co, had announced broad price hikes for its clothing products due to rising input costs. Less than two weeks later, it reversed a decision to increase the price of its socks by ¥100 (US$0.63), and eliminate discounts on purchases of three or more pairs.

After decades of deflation, which conditioned Japanese shoppers to expect flat prices, retailers are struggling with how much of their rising costs they can pass on to customers. Consumer prices, excluding fresh food and other items, climbed 3.2% in September from a year earlier, while household spending is shrinking, reflecting the challenge companies face when seeking to protect margins.

“The fact that they decided not to go ahead with the price increase suggests they were very conscious of consumers’ resistance to higher prices,” said Atsushi Takeda, chief economist at Itochu Research Institute. “It’s no longer just lower-income consumers who are feeling the strain, but consumers somewhat higher up the income scale are also increasingly becoming wary of rising prices.”

Uniqlo’s swift response to the socks price hike followed an outcry on social media from shoppers frustrated by higher prices.

“As socks are an essential everyday item, in Japan we reconsidered our planned price revision,” a Fast Retailing spokesperson said.

See also: Adani flagship returns to profit as newer businesses deliver

title: Tech stocks drop as Alphabet, Samsung disappoint
article:
(Oct 29): Technology shares fell, snapping this week’s rally, after disappointing earnings from two industry heavyweights revived concerns about the billions of dollars companies are pouring into artificial intelligence (AI).

Samsung Electronics Co shares dropped more than 5% after profit missed estimates, dragging down the Kospi Index — a bellwether for the AI trade — by 2.9%. That marked a sharp reversal from Wednesday, when the gauge posted its biggest rally since July as strong earnings from chipmaker SK Hynix Inc fuelled gains across technology stocks.

Alphabet Inc slumped 10% in extended trading after sales underwhelmed, reinforcing investors’ fears that Google is losing ground to AI rivals despite pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology. Futures for the Nasdaq 100 Index slid 1.3%, after the underlying benchmark climbed for the past three days. The broader MSCI Inc’s Asia Pacific equities reversed earlier gains to drop 0.7%.

The news wasn’t all bad as Microsoft Corp shares rose 2.9% in after-hours trading on solid cloud sales, while Oracle Corp earlier surged 11% after issuing a long-term outlook for free cash flow. A gauge of Oracle’s credit risk improved the most in nearly nine months.

The latest earnings have exposed fresh cracks in the AI trade, raising doubts about whether massive spending on the technology can deliver returns quickly enough to justify lofty valuations. The concern is that investment in chips, data centres and other infrastructure is accelerating faster than the revenue needed to generate adequate returns, leaving technology shares vulnerable to further disappointment.

“The divergence in after-hours trading between Alphabet and Microsoft shares highlights growing scrutiny of how big tech companies are funding their ambitious data centre build-outs,” said Hugh Lam, a Sydney-based investment strategist at Betashares Capital Ltd.

See also: Asian stocks rise, Treasuries steady before Fed decision

Elsewhere, shorter-maturity Treasuries held their gains from Wednesday when the Federal Reserve (Fed) held off from raising interest rates, while signalling fewer policy-setting meetings next year. The yield on the rate-sensitive two-year note was at 4.69%.

Meanwhile, oil dropped as traders assessed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran. Global benchmark Brent declined 0.5% to US$114.80 a barrel.

Still, the macro backdrop offered little support for markets as renewed tensions with Iran threatened to lift oil prices, stoke inflation and reinforce the case for keeping borrowing costs elevated.

See also: Tech rally extends to Asia on Anthropic, oil falls

“The Fed appears comfortable being patient for now as financial conditions have evolved broadly in line with expectations,” said Luis Alvarado at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “But patience should not be confused with complacency.”

More central bank decisions are due this week, with the European Central Bank announcing policy Thursday and the Bank of Japan on Friday. Both are expected to keep rates unchanged.

Thursday also brings personal consumption expenditures data, the Fed’s preferred inflation gauge, which will offer fresh clues on price pressures in the economy.

Meanwhile, the Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold its benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%. In their post-meeting statement, policymakers said they hoped incoming data in the coming weeks would help inform their next decision.

Fed chairman Kevin Warsh said officials have “made clear our readiness to act as circumstances require, and we have shown our willingness to act”. Warsh also said the central bank will phase in an adjusted meeting schedule, with plans to hold rate-setting votes at seven out of eight meetings next year.

“Fewer decision meetings plus no forward guidance are a recipe for bigger repricing around each one, and more volatility around rates than markets are currently pricing,” said Ali Hassan, portfolio manager at Santa Fe, New Mexico-based Thornburg Investment Management.

title: Petrobras pumps at record as Iran war upends oil markets
article:
(Oct 29): Brazil’s state-controlled oil producer Petrobras lifted production to a record and ran its refineries near full capacity in the third quarter, helping the country weather disruptions to global energy markets from the Iran war.

Oil and gas output climbed 12% on year to 3.51 million barrels of oil equivalent a day, Petroleo Brasileiro SA, as the company is formally known, said in a filing on Wednesday. Production rose 5.3% compared to the second quarter as Petrobras ramped up new platforms at deep-water fields, including the P-78 and P-79 units at the giant Buzios project.

The floating production and storage vessel Alexandre de Gusmao reached peak production at the Mero field, and there were fewer losses from maintenance shutdowns, Petrobras said.

The growth in production and refining has helped Latin America’s largest economy limit its exposure to the global energy shock. Petrobras ran its refineries at 99% of capacity during the quarter, reaching record diesel production.

Oil production of 2.8 million barrels a day in the quarter puts Petrobras above its implied 2026 guidance and gives the company a higher starting point for 2027, according to Ativa Investimentos analyst Ilan Arbetman, who had flagged the potential in a note ahead of the report.

Brazil has used subsidies and tax cuts to cushion consumers from soaring fuel costs, while Petrobras has kept its refineries running at high rates to supply the domestic market.

See also: Oil jumps with Israeli election and Iran attack report in focus

But with Brent trading above US$110 a barrel and Petrobras fuel prices lagging international benchmarks, pressure is building on the company to raise prices. On Wednesday, Petrobras’s average diesel price at the refinery gate was 3.76 reais (US$0.70) a litre below import parity, a gap of 115%, according to fuel importers association Abicom. Gasoline was 24% below international levels, according to the group.

title: Alphabet’s revenue miss reignites fears over AI spending binge
article:
(Oct 29): Alphabet Inc’s search and advertising sales disappointed in the most recent quarter, reinforcing investors’ fears that Google is losing ground to artificial intelligence (AI) rivals despite pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into the technology.

The Google parent reported sales, excluding partner payouts, of US$111.2 billion ($142.4 billion) for the third quarter, falling short of analysts’ projections. Its advertising revenue from the search engine and related businesses — which accounts for roughly half of overall sales and is critical to financing its massive AI investments — also missed forecasts, growing at the slowest pace in five quarters.

Shares of Alphabet slid 10% in late trading on Wednesday. The company’s performance stood in particularly stark contrast to rival Microsoft Corp, which reported growth in its cloud business that surpassed Wall Street’s expectations while keeping its spending in check, stoking a rally in its stock.

The pressure on Alphabet chief executive officer Sundar Pichai to justify the more than US$1 trillion that Google is facing in future payments on resources such as data centres, computing and energy to power his AI ambitions is mounting. “This quarter feels like a moment of truth for Alphabet: Either Pichai and his team fix the way the company monetizes AI, or the giant risks losing its leadership in several of its core businesses in the near future,” said Thomas Monteiro, senior analyst at Investing.com.

“Until Google shows it can charge for AI the way it once charged for search ads,” he said, every capital spending forecast it issues is going to “read less like ambition and more like a bill”.

See also: Memory stocks lost their shine despite strong earnings

Google’s sprint to build AI infrastructure for both itself and customers has sent the firm’s capital expenditures soaring to record levels. The firm is working to overhaul popular products such as the search engine, YouTube and Gmail with AI. But those efforts have yet to yield the kind of revenue the investors want to see to justify all the spending.

Google’s overall services revenue totalled US$96.3 billion in the third quarter, below estimates for US$98.4 billion. YouTube advertising sales of US$11.2 billion also fell below projections.

Adding to investors’ concerns: Alphabet chief business officer Philipp Schindler said in an earnings call with investors late Wednesday that the growing popularity of AI Mode, a new tab in Google Search, took a toll on the company’s results. Those queries have “lower monetization”, Schindler said, though he noted that the company was optimistic and has plans to bring more ads to that part of the search engine.

See also: Instagram ramps up video strategy in escalating TikTok, YouTube rivalry

In the meantime, Google’s AI bets are getting even more expensive. By the end of the third quarter, Google’s future commitments to buy resources such as computing power and energy totalled US$924 billion. Upcoming obligations such as data-centre leases that haven’t yet commenced hit US$152 billion, bringing the company’s total future obligations to well over US$1 trillion.

For the second quarter in a row, the company posted negative free cash flow, something it had, up until now, never seen since going public.

“Search still generates the bulk of Alphabet’s cash, and two straight quarters of negative free cash flow show the pure AI math isn’t working right now,” said Anders Bylund, contributing tech analyst at the Motley Fool.

Alphabet said in July that capital expenditures will reach as much as US$205 billion this year, more than double what it spent last year. AI requires massive amounts of computing power, and Google is racing to build data centres so it can meet demand for AI from consumers, businesses and its own employees.

Alphabet’s equity investments also weighed on the company’s bottom line. Those stakes posted an US$8.7 billion loss, in large part due to Alphabet’s SpaceX position. That’s a sharp reversal from the gains it saw a year earlier and the windfall in the second quarter that was mainly driven by SpaceX and an investment in a private company that Bloomberg later identified as Anthropic PBC.

Its third-quarter net income was US$2.12 a share, falling far below Wall Street’s estimate of US$2.99.

One bright spot in the report was Google Cloud, which is seen as a key gauge of demand for the company’s AI products and hosting services. The division reported sales of US$30.7 billion and profit of US$11.1 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of US$29.1 billion in revenue and US$9.8 billion in profit. Among the unit’s biggest customers are startups such as Anthropic that compete with Google in the AI race.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

“Cloud is booming, but many of its best customers are building assistants that are already beating Google with consumers,” Monteiro wrote. “Right now, Alphabet earns more selling AI to its rivals than using it itself, and that gap should keep growing over the next few quarters unless its models change drastically, and quickly.”

Over the past few years, Google has been working to reinvent its search engine for the AI age, trying to keep consumers in the habit of relying on its answers even as chatbots from OpenAI and Anthropic become more popular. The company now delivers AI-generated answers in response to many searches, a shift that has had major implications for businesses that have traditionally relied on the search giant for traffic and advertising revenue.

Google has worked particularly hard on building an edge by generating more personalised responses to questions, leveraging years of information about its users. In recent months, though, the company has fallen behind Anthropic and OpenAI in developing AI coding tools. Google recently released Gemini 4, which it says excels in areas such as coding and cybersecurity, though some employees fear the company has yet to fully catch up.

Hours before its earnings call, Google announced yet another new AI model known as Carbon, a potential answer to the critics who’ve called for the company to speed up the pace of AI development.

“We have more models coming soon,” Pichai told analysts on the call, “including more efficient versions to help developers optimise for speed and cost and to deploy across our billions of users”.

title: Oil declines as traders parse signs of fresh diplomacy on Iran
article:
(Oct 29) : Oil dropped as traders weighed fresh diplomatic efforts in the Middle East to avert a potential restart of US military strikes on Iran.

West Texas Intermediate fell toward US$102 a barrel, after rising almost 3% in the previous session, while Brent closed near US$115. Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said that Tehran continued to give diplomacy chance, and the Wall Street Journal reported US Vice President JD Vance had reached out to Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the nation’s top security body.

President Donald Trump told Axios on Wednesday that negotiations were taking place through mediators but stressed he didn’t know whether they would bear fruit. “We need to finish the job — either through a deal or another way — we will find out if negotiations can succeed,” he was quoted as saying.

Global crude benchmark Brent has rallied by 11% this month, touching the highest since April, as the conflict dragged on. The surge has heaped pressure on consumers and presented a challenge to central bankers seeking to contain inflation. While the Federal Reserve opted to keep policy unchanged this week, traders expect officials to resume tightening in December.

US voters will go to the polls on Nov. 3 for midterm elections amid signs that there’ll be a slump in support for Republicans. President Trump has given frequent signals that he may opt to resume a military campaign against Tehran after ballots have been cast, possibly in coordination with Israel’s forces.

In Israel, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu edged ahead of opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot after a tightly fought election, although neither has a clear path toward forming a government. It will be days before President Isaac Herzog chooses who gets the chance to cobble together a new ruling coalition.

See also: Stocks edge higher after Fed as Oracle surges 11%

title: Stocks edge higher after Fed as Oracle surges 11%
article:
(Oct 29) : Stocks edged up as the Federal Reserve held rates steady and refrained from offering a clear signal on whether it will hike in December.

The S&P 500 rose 0.3%. Oracle Corp. soared 11% on a long-term outlook for free cash flow. Microsoft Corp. jumped in extended trading on solid cloud sales. Alphabet Inc. sank on disappointing results. Short-dated Treasuries gained. An oil rally waned in late hours as the Wall Street Journal said US Vice President JD Vance reached out to an Iranian hard-liner to revive peace talks.

The Federal Open Market Committee voted 10-2 to hold its benchmark federal funds rate in a range of 3.75% to 4%. In their post-meeting statement, policymakers said they hoped incoming data would help inform their next decision.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh noted officials have “made clear our readiness to act as circumstances require, and we have shown our willingness to act.”

“The Fed appears comfortable being patient for now as financial conditions have evolved broadly in line with expectations,” said Luis Alvarado at Wells Fargo Investment Institute. “But patience should not be confused with complacency.”

Warsh also said the central bank will phase in an adjusted meeting schedule, with plans to hold rate-setting votes at seven out of eight meetings next year.

See also: Oil holds biggest gain in week as Saudi attacks fan supply risks

The Fed’s new meeting schedule appears consistent with Warsh’s push for less forward guidance and less frequent signaling to markets, according to Tony Miano at Wells Fargo Investment Institute.

“The biggest change from the Fed today wasn’t to policy rates but rather to the forward calendar of making decisions,” said Ian Lyngen at BMO Capital Markets. “The most relevant question at the moment is what meetings will be devoted to things other than potentially changing rates.”

If nothing else, short-dated notes rose as Warsh left the market with the impression that one hike — in September — was effective thus far, Lyngen added. That would imply that following a December move, a third hike might not be seen as necessary, he noted.

See also: Asian stocks to slide on tech rout, bonds rally

While traders maintained bets officials will raise rates in December, they trimmed wagers on additional hikes in 2027. Futures markets are no longer fully pricing three more hikes this cycle.

title: Mi Material closes at $1.82 on first day of trading; Stabilisation manager bought 1.5 mil shares at IPO price of $1.80
article:
Mi Material closed at $1.82 on its first day of trading on Oct 28, valuing the company at $900 million.

Mi Material’s share price debuted at $1.80, which is equivalent to its initial public offering (IPO) price, and reached an intra-day high of $1.86. At the close of trading on Oct 28, more than 10.7 million shares changed hands.

On Oct 27, Mi Material announced that its IPO was just 2.2 times subscribed. The public offer of slightly over 6.2 million shares was just 1.3 times taken, while the international offer of nearly 71.3 million shares was 2.2 times subscribed.

Mi Material’s stabilisation manager, CGS International, has purchased 1.5 million shares at $1.80 on Oct 28. With this latest purchase, the stabilisation manager has left with just 3.5 million shares under the grant of over-allotment option.

OCBC and CGS International are the joint global coordinators, bookrunners and underwriters for this IPO.
